pre_condition: The caller provides exclusive mutable access to a prepared destination LoadedVm and does not concurrently start, resume, or mutate guest execution state during this call.

saved_state is an accepted snapshot for this destination: its format, architecture, component identities, resource requirements, and compatibility constraints have already been validated, or LoadedVm::restore is contractually responsible for rejecting them.
The destination already has valid prepared memory, capacity, host-resource bindings, and backend configuration; these destination-owned values are not implicitly snapshot-owned.

The VM is stopped before any snapshot state becomes observable, unless temporarily_stop_vps and the enclosing restore protocol provide an equivalent no-execution guarantee covering the entire call. This requirement is not established by the supplied body.

If restore_time is Some((downtime, saved_frequency, saved_apic_frequency)), downtime is a permitted restore transformation, the destination exposes the required clock frequencies, the destination TSC frequency equals saved_frequency, and, when saved_apic_frequency is Some, the destination APIC frequency equals it.
Stable VP identities used by the snapshot can be mapped to destination VPs; destination VPs absent from the snapshot have valid initial or default state.
post_condition: On Ok(()), the VM is at a pre-execution observation boundary: guest VPs are stopped and remain prevented from executing by restore_start_guard until the surrounding protocol deliberately releases that guard.
The guest-observable projection of all snapshot-owned active state equals the accepted saved_state projection after applying exactly the transformations authorized by restore_time.

Pending or deferred component state remains pending or deferred unless the accepted snapshot and component restore contracts explicitly require activation; successful restore does not by itself imply readiness, resume, or deferred-work completion.

Saved VP state is restored by stable VP identity. A destination VP represented in the snapshot has the corresponding saved state; a destination VP not represented in the snapshot retains a valid destination initial or default state rather than receiving another VP's state.
If restore_time is None, no downtime adjustment is intentionally applied by this body.

If restore_time is Some((downtime, frequency, saved_apic_frequency)), restored state-unit time is advanced by downtime; on x86_64, restored VP TSC state is advanced by downtime using frequency and an APIC frequency selected according to the restore policy; backend snapshot time is advanced by downtime.

Prepared destination memory, compatibility facts, capacity, external-resource bindings, and host operational state are preserved except for changes explicitly required by documented restore callee contracts.
Successful return does not assert that the VM has resumed, is ready to resume, or has completed post-restore initialization.
failure_condition: Err means that at least one frequency query or check, frequency-setting operation, snapshot restore operation, time-advance operation, or required backend query failed.

This body provides no rollback or failure-atomicity mechanism. On Err, destination state may be partially mutated: the TSC frequency setter may have run, snapshot components may have been partly restored, and one or more clock domains may have been advanced.

Failures before the final temporarily_stop_vps call do not cause this body to install restore_start_guard. Safety after such a failure therefore depends on the entry-state stop invariant and callee failure contracts.
The caller must not treat Err as preserving the original destination state unless separate contracts establish transactional behavior for every completed mutation.

abstract_state.snapshot_owned_active_state: Guest-relevant active component, device, processor, and architectural state represented by the accepted snapshot.
abstract_state.snapshot_owned_pending_state: Snapshot-represented pending or deferred component state, including state that must remain inactive until a later lifecycle phase.
abstract_state.vp_state_by_identity: A partial map from stable VP identity to saved VP state, combined with valid initial or default state for destination VPs outside the map.
abstract_state.guest_time: Snapshot time transformed by the permitted downtime adjustment, separately projected across state units, VP clocks where applicable, and backend snapshot time.
abstract_state.execution_state: Stopped at successful return, with execution inhibited by an owned guard.
abstract_state.destination_owned_state: Prepared memory topology, capacity, compatibility decisions, external-resource bindings, and host operational details not represented as snapshot-owned values.

abstraction.projection: Project the concrete LoadedVm into guest-observable snapshot-owned active state, pending/deferred status, VP state keyed by stable identity, guest-visible clock values, and whether any VP can execute. Compare that projection with the accepted saved_state projection transformed only by the authorized downtime operation. Exclude destination-owned preparation and host-runtime details unless a component contract explicitly classifies a field as snapshot-owned.
preserved_state: Destination VPs not selected by a stable identity in the snapshot retain valid initial or default state.
Prepared destination memory and capacity remain destination-owned.
Compatibility decisions and external-resource bindings remain destination-owned.
Pending or deferred state remains pending or deferred absent an explicit activation rule.
Host operational details remain unchanged except where a documented restore primitive necessarily updates hidden backend bookkeeping.

abstraction.observation_boundary: The exact boundary is the instant Ok(()) is produced after temporarily_stop_vps().await has completed and the resulting guard has been stored in self.restore_start_guard, but before the caller can release or replace that guard, resume VPs, or perform later readiness work. No intermediate state during the async call is included in the success abstraction, provided no VP can execute during those intermediate states.

implementation_assessment.disposition: Equality is checked by this body. The setter is observationally redundant at the numeric level but may have backend side effects; preservation of destination-owned state remains unproven.

implementation_assessment.claim: APIC frequency handling is consistent for snapshots without a saved APIC frequency.

On x86_64, a destination lacking an APIC frequency can pass the initial checks and fail only after restore and state_units time advancement, leaving partial state. This may be intentional backend validation timing, but it is a material bug hypothesis requiring policy clarification.

implementation_assessment.claim: Non-x86_64 restores consistently interpret the frequency tuple.

implementation_assessment.disposition: Uncertain. The generic partition interface may intentionally expose these clocks on all supported architectures, but architecture-specific contracts are required.

implementation_assessment.claim: Failure is atomic.
implementation_assessment.evidence: Several fallible mutations occur in sequence without rollback.
implementation_assessment.disposition: Not established and apparently false under ordinary non-transactional callee semantics. The caller-facing contract should explicitly permit partial mutation unless stronger callee guarantees are supplied.

implementation_assessment.claim: Profiling operations do not affect correctness.
implementation_assessment.evidence: Profile spans wrap restoration, time advancement, and VP stopping, and their complete calls are not fallible in the shown code.
implementation_assessment.disposition: Reasonable framing assumption, but formally it remains an assumption unless ProfileSpan is specified as observationally irrelevant.

candidate_variants.name: Strong transactional stopped restore
candidate_variants.semantic_difference: Requires the VM to remain stopped for the entire call and requires any Err to preserve the complete pre-call destination state, including clock domains and component state.
candidate_variants.discriminator: Inject a failure after each mutating step and compare a full pre/post destination-state projection while concurrently asserting that no VP instruction retires.

candidate_variants.name: Baseline stopped-success restore
candidate_variants.semantic_difference: Requires exact transformed snapshot projection and a held stop guard only on Ok; Err may leave partial state that must be torn down or treated as unusable.
candidate_variants.discriminator: Inject a failure after state_units.advance_time. Partial mutation is permitted, but no successful result may expose a runnable VP or an incorrect transformed projection.

candidate_variants.name: Weaker lifecycle-only restore
candidate_variants.semantic_difference: Requires only that accepted component restore operations and requested time adjustments complete and that a stop guard is stored; it does not require observational equality for all snapshot-owned state, stable VP identity behavior, or preservation of unmatched VP defaults.
candidate_variants.discriminator: Restore a snapshot into a destination whose VP enumeration order differs. This variant can pass when operations report success even if VP states are swapped; the baseline variant cannot.

candidate_variants.name: Destination-APIC fallback policy
candidate_variants.semantic_difference: Interprets saved_apic_frequency None as authorization to use the destination APIC frequency for x86_64 downtime adjustment, while still requiring that frequency to be available before any restore mutation.
candidate_variants.discriminator: Use a snapshot with no saved APIC frequency against backends that expose, omit, or vary destination APIC frequency and verify whether validation occurs before self.restore.

candidate_variants.name: No-APIC-adjustment legacy policy
candidate_variants.semantic_difference: Interprets saved_apic_frequency None as meaning that APIC time must not be adjusted from snapshot state, rather than substituting the destination frequency.
candidate_variants.discriminator: Restore a legacy snapshot with None and nonzero downtime, then inspect guest APIC timer progression relative to TSC progression.

contract.pre_condition: The caller provides exclusive mutable access to a prepared destination LoadedVm and prevents concurrent start, resume, or mutation of guest execution state. The supplied saved_state is an accepted snapshot whose format, architecture, component identities, resource requirements, and compatibility have already been validated, unless LoadedVm::restore is explicitly responsible for rejecting them. Destination memory, capacity, host-resource bindings, and backend configuration are valid and remain destination-owned. No VP may execute from the first restore-related mutation through successful return; this must follow from an entry invariant, an existing guard, or a surrounding lifecycle protocol because this body stops VPs only at the end. Stable saved VP identities must be mappable to destination VPs, while unmatched destination VPs must have valid initial or default state. If restore_time is Some((downtime, saved_frequency, saved_apic_frequency)), downtime is an authorized restore transformation and the required destination clock frequencies are available and compatible.
contract.post_condition: On Ok(()), the VM is at a pre-execution boundary: all VPs are stopped and remain inhibited by restore_start_guard until the surrounding protocol deliberately releases it. The guest-observable projection of snapshot-owned active state equals the accepted saved_state projection after exactly the transformation authorized by restore_time. Pending or deferred snapshot state remains pending or deferred unless an explicit component contract requires activation. Saved VP state is selected by stable identity, and destination VPs absent from the snapshot retain valid initial or default state. If restore_time is None, this body intentionally applies no downtime adjustment. If restore_time is Some, state-unit time, x86_64 VP clock state, and backend snapshot time are advanced by downtime according to their contracts. Prepared destination memory, capacity, compatibility decisions, external-resource bindings, and host operational state are preserved except where an explicit restore contract permits mutation. Success does not imply resume, readiness, or completion of later post-restore work.
contract.failure_condition: Err indicates failure of a frequency query or compatibility check, frequency setting, snapshot restoration, time advancement, or required backend query. The body provides no rollback or failure atomicity: destination state may be partially mutated, including an updated TSC configuration, partially restored components, or partially advanced clock domains. Errors before temporarily_stop_vps do not install restore_start_guard, so safety depends on the entry-state no-execution invariant and callee failure contracts. Callers must not assume that Err preserves the pre-call destination state or permits retry unless separate contracts establish those properties.

candidate_variants.name: Strong transactional stopped restore
candidate_variants.semantic_difference: Requires continuous stopping throughout the call and requires every Err to preserve the complete pre-call destination state, including components and clock domains.
candidate_variants.discriminator: Inject a failure after each mutating step, compare the complete pre-call and post-failure projections, and concurrently assert that no VP instruction retires.

candidate_variants.name: Baseline stopped-success restore
candidate_variants.semantic_difference: Requires exact transformed snapshot projection and a held stop guard only on Ok; Err may leave partial state that must be torn down or treated as unusable.
candidate_variants.discriminator: Inject failure after state_units.advance_time. Partial mutation is permitted, but no successful result may expose a runnable VP or incorrect transformed projection.

candidate_variants.name: Weaker lifecycle-only restore
candidate_variants.semantic_difference: Requires only successful completion of delegated restore and requested time adjustments plus storage of a stop guard; it does not guarantee observational equality, stable VP identity mapping, or preservation of unmatched VP defaults.
candidate_variants.discriminator: Restore into a destination whose VP enumeration order differs. This variant may pass when operations report success even if VP states are swapped; the baseline variant cannot.

candidate_variants.name: Destination APIC fallback policy
candidate_variants.semantic_difference: Interprets saved_apic_frequency None as authorization to use the destination APIC frequency for x86_64 downtime adjustment, while requiring that frequency to be available before any restore mutation.
candidate_variants.discriminator: Use a snapshot with no saved APIC frequency against backends that expose, omit, or vary destination APIC frequency and verify whether rejection occurs before self.restore.

candidate_variants.name: No APIC adjustment legacy policy
candidate_variants.semantic_difference: Interprets saved_apic_frequency None as requiring no APIC adjustment from snapshot state rather than substitution of the destination frequency.
candidate_variants.discriminator: Restore a legacy snapshot with None and nonzero downtime, then inspect guest APIC timer progression relative to TSC progression.

metadata.parse_error: assessment disposition must be supported, challenged, or unknown

contract.pre_condition: The caller provides exclusive mutable access to a prepared destination LoadedVm and prevents concurrent start, resume, or mutation of guest execution state. The supplied saved_state is an accepted snapshot whose format, architecture, component identities, resource requirements, and compatibility have already been validated, unless LoadedVm::restore is explicitly responsible for rejecting them. Destination memory, capacity, host-resource bindings, and backend configuration are valid and remain destination-owned. No VP may execute from the first restore-related mutation through successful return; this must follow from an entry invariant, an existing guard, or a surrounding lifecycle protocol because this body stops VPs only at the end. Stable saved VP identities must be mappable to destination VPs, while unmatched destination VPs must have valid initial or default state. If restore_time is Some((downtime, saved_frequency, saved_apic_frequency)), downtime is an authorized restore transformation and the required destination clock frequencies are available and compatible.
contract.post_condition: On Ok(()), the VM is at a pre-execution boundary: all VPs are stopped and remain inhibited by restore_start_guard until the surrounding protocol deliberately releases it. The guest-observable projection of snapshot-owned active state equals the accepted saved_state projection after exactly the transformation authorized by restore_time. Pending or deferred snapshot state remains pending or deferred unless an explicit component contract requires activation. Saved VP state is selected by stable identity, and destination VPs absent from the snapshot retain valid initial or default state. If restore_time is None, this body intentionally applies no downtime adjustment. If restore_time is Some, state-unit time, x86_64 VP clock state, and backend snapshot time are advanced by downtime according to their contracts. Prepared destination memory, capacity, compatibility decisions, external-resource bindings, and host operational state are preserved except where an explicit restore contract permits mutation. Success does not imply resume, readiness, or completion of later post-restore work.
contract.failure_condition: Err indicates failure of a frequency query or compatibility check, frequency setting, snapshot restoration, time advancement, or required backend query. The body provides no rollback or failure atomicity: destination state may be partially mutated, including an updated TSC configuration, partially restored components, or partially advanced clock domains. Errors before temporarily_stop_vps do not install restore_start_guard, so safety depends on the entry-state no-execution invariant and callee failure contracts. Callers must not assume that Err preserves the pre-call destination state or permits retry unless separate contracts establish those properties.

abstraction.name: StoppedRestoredGuestProjection
abstraction.abstract_state: A tuple consisting of snapshot-owned active guest state, snapshot-owned pending or deferred state, a partial map of stable VP identity to VP state augmented by valid defaults for unmatched destination VPs, guest-visible clock domains, an execution-inhibited flag, and destination-owned preparation and host-runtime state.
abstraction.projection: Project the concrete LoadedVm into guest-observable snapshot-owned active state, pending or deferred status, VP state keyed by stable identity, guest-visible clock values, and whether any VP can execute. Compare this with the accepted saved_state projection transformed only by the authorized downtime operation. Exclude destination-owned memory preparation, capacity, compatibility decisions, external-resource bindings, and host-runtime details unless an explicit component contract classifies a field as snapshot-owned.
abstraction.preserved_state: Destination VPs not selected by stable snapshot identity retain valid initial or default state. Prepared destination memory, capacity, compatibility decisions, external-resource bindings, and host operational details remain destination-owned. Pending or deferred state remains pending or deferred absent an explicit activation rule.
abstraction.hidden_representation: Concrete state_units internals, partition and partition_unit backend structures, stop-guard representation and nesting, component serialization formats, restore dispatch ordering, profiling spans, and backend bookkeeping that does not affect the defined guest-observable projection.
abstraction.observation_boundary: The instant Ok(()) is produced after temporarily_stop_vps().await completes and its guard is stored in self.restore_start_guard, but before the caller can release or replace that guard, resume VPs, or perform later readiness work. Intermediate async states are outside the success abstraction only if no VP can execute during them.
